problem_definition:
Formal setting: Given a target model $M_p$ and a draft model $M_q$, speculative decoding generates draft tokens using $M_q$ and verifies them in parallel using $M_p$ to approximate the target distribution $p(y|x, y_{<t})$ while accelerating inference.. Inputs: Image and text prompts, past verified tokens, and target model probabilities. Outputs: Draft token probabilities and accepted draft tokens for accelerated generation

Problem statement: Existing speculative decoding drafting methods for Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) exhibit scenario-specific performance fluctuations, making it difficult to select a single drafting approach that consistently accelerates inference across diverse multimodal inputs.. Why it matters: LVLMs require significantly higher inference time due to image token processing, making acceleration critical for real-world deployment. Current drafting methods either ignore visual context or require additional training, failing to adapt to varying turn-taking, task types, and out-of-distribution scenarios.
challenge: Existing speculative decoding drafting methods for Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) exhibit scenario-specific performance fluctuations, making it difficult to select a single drafting approach that consistently accelerates inference across diverse multimodal inputs..
target_title: TABED: Test-Time Adaptive Ensemble Drafting for Robust Speculative Decoding in LVLMs
